cards.design_implication: Design protocols may incorporate interface engineering of exfoliation substrates to decouple adhesion requirements during material assembly.
does_not_establish: Universal success across all heterogeneous material systems.
cards.evidence_excerpt: An ef<sup>fi</sup>cient and high-yield fabrication process could be achieved if the adhesion at the <sup>fl</sup>ake-substrate interface can be optimized independently during the exfoliation and transfer steps. Here, we report a strategy that achieves this objective.
limitations: Applicability is explicitly described for PVA on SiO2.
The mechanism is proposed and demonstrated in the context of graphene and layered materials.
cards.statement: The use of a sub-5 nm polymeric film (PVA) on SiO2 allows the adhesion strength for exfoliation and the adhesion strength for layer transfer to be optimized independently.

cards.design_implication: Experimental designs might include comparative analysis of flake dimensions and yield against established conventional exfoliation methods to validate process improvements.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Figure 2e compares the dimensions of the 100 largest PAGE <sup>fl</sup>akes against those produced using the conventional method. We obtained these <sup>fl</sup>akes from 33 PAGE samples and 77 conventional exfoliation samples.
limitations: Comparison was restricted to the 100 largest flakes.
Sample counts (33 vs 77) were inconsistent across methods in this specific analysis.
cards.statement: Exfoliation efficiency was evaluated by comparing the dimensions of the 100 largest flakes from PAGE samples against those from conventional exfoliation samples.
